Two reports built on cetacean survey data from the NOAA Pacific Islands
Fisheries Science Center. They are meant to be read in order: the first maps
what the public sighting archive can show, the second uses line-transect data
to do what that archive cannot.

### [Seasonal cetacean sighting records](cetacean-seasonal-map.html)

Where cetaceans were recorded across the Hawaiian Islands EEZ, month by month,
from nine survey cruises between 2009 and 2017. An animated map over
bathymetry, and an account of why a record of sightings without a record of
effort can describe distribution but not abundance.

### [A density surface model for humpback whales](humpback-dsm.html)

Line-transect data from the winter 2020 survey, reprocessed with PIFSC's own
software into 10 km segments, fitted with a detection function and a Tweedie
GAM over depth and space, and predicted across the study area. The resulting
abundance estimate is compared against the published design-based figure for
the same survey.

---

Code and data sources for both are in the
[repository](https://github.com/TheophileMt92/hawaii-cetacean-seasonality).
Survey data collected by NOAA Pacific Islands Fisheries Science Center,
Protected Species Division.
